tools.name: ai_aistatus
tools.description: Returns whether the PRTG AI Agent service is registered with the Windows Service Control Manager, whether it is running, and whether the agent is connected to PRTG. This endpoint is experimental. For more information, see the [PRTG API v2 Overview: Endpoint Maturity](../overview/index.html#endpoint-maturity). This endpoint is disabled by default. Enable it with the `aianalyzeendpoint` feature toggle. While disabled, the endpoint stays visible in this reference but returns `403 FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED` for every request. The answer comes from the Windows Service Control Manager, not from the PRTG AI Agent. Nothing is sent to the agent, because a question you have to ask the agent cannot tell you the agent is missing. The response carries `registration`, `state` and `connected` together, in one round trip: a service that is not installed also reports `state: stopped` here, and `registration` is what tells that apart from an installed-but-stopped service. `state` comes from the Windows Service Control Manager and `connected` from the PRTG side of the transport. They answer different questions: a service can be running while nothing is attached, which is what a crash-looping or blocked agent looks like. The PRTG AI Agent ships only as a Windows service, so this endpoint is unsupported on every other platform.

params.name: offset
params.description: Use offset to define which results are returned. For example, if you enter 0 for offset and 100 for limit, the API returns results 0 to 99. The index is zero based. For more information, see Overview: Pagination .

params.name: limit
params.description: Enter the number of objects that the request returns. The maximum number of objects is 3000. If you enter 0, the request returns up to 3000 objects.

params.name: filter
params.description: Define filters to filter the results. For more information, see Overview: Filter .

params.name: include
params.description: By default, this endpoint only returns the most relevant information about the requested users. You can include additional parameters: | Parameter | Description | Example | | ------ | ------ | ------ |  | `all_sections` Individual settings sections | Explicitly request one, multiple, or all settings sections. | `include=all_sections` `include=usercontrol,commentgroup` | | `*` | A wildcard that includes the all_sections, usercontrol, and commentgroup parameters. | `include=*`| For more information, see the [Overview: Includes](../overview/index.html#includes).

tools.name: users_modify-apikey
tools.description: Edits an API key. Required: id. Optional: access_level, description, name. Partial update.

params.name: id
params.description: Enter the ID of the API key that you want to edit.

params.name: access_level
params.description: The access level of the API key.

params.name: description
params.description: A textual description of the API key.

params.name: name
params.description: The name of the API key.

tools.name: users_multi-pause-request
tools.description: Pauses all user accounts that match a filter. Required: filter. Returns array of ActionResult.

params.name: filter
params.description: Define filters to limit the results that the request returns.

tools.name: users_multi-resume
tools.description: Resumes all user accounts that match a filter. Required: filter. Returns array of ActionResult.

params.name: filter
params.description: Define filters to limit and specify the results that the request returns.

tools.name: users_reset-password
tools.description: Set a new password for a user account with the token from the password reset process. **Note:** This route is not available when using PPHM. Required: password, token, username.

params.name: password
params.description: The new password for the user account.

params.name: token
params.description: The token from the password reset process.

params.name: username
params.description: The user name of the user account whose password you want to change.

tools.name: users_trigger-password-reset
tools.description: Triggers the password reset process for a user account. **Note:** This route is not available when using PPHM. Required: username.

params.name: username
params.description: The user name of the user account that you want to initiate the password reset process for.

tools.name: users_api-keys_create
tools.description: Creates a new API key. Required: id, access_level, name. Optional: description. Returns the new CreateApikeyResponse.

params.name: id
params.description: Enter the ID of the user that you want to create an API key for. Enter 'me' if you want to create an API key for your own user account.

params.name: access_level
params.description: The access level of the new API key.

params.name: description
params.description: A textual description of the new API key.

params.name: name
params.description: The name of the new API key.

tools.name: users_api-keys_list
tools.description: Returns a list of API keys that belong to a user account. Required: id.

params.name: id
params.description: Enter the ID of the user that you want to get a list of API keys for. Enter 'me' if you want a list of your own API keys.

tools.name: users_pause_user
tools.description: Pauses a user account. Required: id.

params.name: id
params.description: Enter the ID of the user account that you want to pause.

tools.name: users_resume_user
tools.description: Resumes a user account. Required: id.

params.name: id
params.description: Enter the ID of the user account that you want to resume.

novel_features.name: Fleet alarms
novel_features.description: See every down, warning and unusual sensor across all of your clients' PRTG cores in one list: worst state first (down, warning, unusual, acknowledged), then higher priority, then oldest.

novel_features.name: Fleet status
novel_features.description: One row per client core with reachability and sensor counts by state, worst first.

novel_features.name: Fleet handoff
novel_features.description: What changed across all cores since a point in time: new alarms, recoveries, and new acknowledgements or pauses with who and why.

novel_features.name: Fleet silenced
novel_features.description: Everything someone paused or acknowledged across all cores, with who, when, until when and why, flagging indefinite ones left too long.

novel_features.name: Fleet drift
novel_features.description: PRTG estate hygiene across cores: versions behind your newest core, expiring licenses or maintenance, sensor overuse, disconnected probes, rejected API keys and unreachable servers.

novel_features.name: Fleet acknowledge
novel_features.description: Acknowledge matching down sensors on every core at once with a ticket message; previews per core and sends only with --yes (the API key needs the Acknowledge access level).

novel_features.name: Fleet maintenance pause
novel_features.description: Pause matching devices, groups, sensors or probes on every core for a maintenance window; previews per core and sends only with --yes (Write access level).

novel_features.name: Fleet maintenance resume
novel_features.description: Resume matching objects on every core after maintenance and optionally trigger an immediate scan; previews per core and sends only with --yes (Write access level).

novel_features.name: Fleet sync
novel_features.description: Refresh the offline mirror of every registered core in one run, each into its own isolated store.

novel_features.name: Fleet exec
novel_features.description: Run any read-only API v2 query on every core and get one merged table with a core column.
